newsitem.title: UK: Transaero to start Manchester-Moscow B737 services.
newsitem.headline: Transaero to start Manchester-Moscow B737 services.

text.p: Privately-owned Russian airline Transaero said it will launch twice-weekly, non-stop scheduled services between Manchester and Moscow on July 1.
It said in a statement that Boeing 737 aircraft will be used, offering up to 1.5 tonnes' cargo capacity on each flight.
Transaero's new services will replace flights operated by Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines, which withdrew from the Manchester-Moscow route at the end of last year, the statement added.

The Manchester service will connect with Transaero flights to 29 other cities in Russia, the CIS, Europe and the United States using a fleet of aircraft including five Boeing 737s, five Boeing 757s, three DC-10s and a Russian-built Ilyushin IL0-86.

The airline, which first began passenger and cargo operations in Russia in 1991, said it uses Moscow's Sheremetyevo 1 Airport as a cargo hub to growing numbers of commercial destinations within Russia.
Last year, Transaero carried 3,616 tonnes of cargo on international, domestic and charter services -- 257 percent more than the previous year when 1,402 tonnes were flown.
Of the total, 1,276 tonnes was flown on scheduled international services, 2,294 on scheduled domestic flights and 46 tonnes on charter flights.

"Freight forwarders and shippers in the Manchester region have been without quality direct air services to Moscow for some time and Transaero is delighted to offer such services again," said the airline's deputy chairman, Gregory Gurtovoy.

"The service will present opportunities for cargo originating in the north of England to fly out of a northern airport, instead of being trucked south to London to catch Moscow-bound flights. Manchester flights will be increased on demand," he added"
Transaero said it is working closely with Latvian airline, Riair, which currently flies five weekly Boeing 737 services from London-Gatwick to Riga and Moscow.
A Transaero aircraft is used on this , which is operated by Riair from Gatwick to Riga and by Transaero on the final sector to Moscow's Sheremetyevo 1 Airport.
